still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

The eleven 2034 state bans on weight-indication incretin prescribing under age 12, and the seven-state in-person rule for low-BMI adult prescriptions, are unchanged; no state has added or repealed one. Congress has still not legislated a permanent Medicare obesity benefit, and the Bridge pilot has not been revived.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Ever minus current: 45.0 − 35.5 = 9.5% of adults used and are off now, unchanged from 2034, because public coverage pulled lapsed users back as fast as new users stopped. Ever-used rose 7.5 points, all first-time users. About 44% of current users are on a second or later course (15.6 points). Another 3.2 points cycled and are off again, so (15.6 + 3.2) / 45 ≈ 41.8% of ever-users have cycled. The remaining 6.3 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence near one-third on full-dose weight regimens (slightly better, ~38%, among Medicaid and Medicare oral users with $0–$10 copays) and restart within a year of 36–47%, at the high end for the publicly covered. Planned drug holidays (below) count as continuing use. Age check: 0.20×19 + 0.33×34 + 0.24×46 + 0.23×41 = 3.8 + 11.2 + 11.0 + 9.4 = 35.5. Income thirds average 35.5. The bottom third gained most (+11.5) once Medicaid coverage became mandatory. 35.5% of ~276M adults ≈ 98.0M users, up ~21M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~28.0M (29%), Medicaid ~10.0M (10%), commercial ~14.5M (15%), legitimate cash ~31.0M (32%), imported/counterfeit ~14.5M (15%). Sum 98.0M. Public programmes, at 38.0M (39%), are now the largest payer category. Cash breakdown: ~12.5M cash weight users (down 1.5M as older and poorer users moved to public plans), ~11.0M longevity/'metabolic health', ~4.0M calm/focus, ~1.8M Reset, ~1.7M AUD. Sum 31.0M. About 19M current users have a BMI under 30 and ~6M under 25; the lean are now disproportionately cash or gray. Adult obesity is ~30.3%. Adults with obesity who have never used fell from ~19% to ~14%, concentrated now among uninsured working-age adults in non-expansion states (Texas, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi) who earn too much for Medicaid and too little for $149 a month. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s (12–17s ~3.0%, mostly Medicaid adolescents on semaglutide or the Wegovy pill under EPSDT). 6–11 liraglutide use is ~0.12%, unchanged under the ban map. About 58% of children live with a current user and ~6.5M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Under the April 2035 CMS final rule, anti-obesity medications used for chronic obesity (BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with a weight-related comorbidity) are no longer treated as excluded 'agents for weight loss'. Medicaid has had to cover them since Oct 2035 and Part D plans since Jan 2036, behind prior authorisation and oral-first step therapy. Medicare reaches ~28.0M users: ~15.5M through the older diabetes/CV/CKD/OSA/dementia-risk codes and ~12.5M through the new obesity route. Prices follow manufacturer agreements of $149/month for orals and $245 for weekly injectables. FICTIONAL arithmetic: average net ≈ 0.6 × $149 + 0.4 × $245 ≈ $187. 28.0M × $187 × 12 ≈ $62.8B gross Part D incretin spend in 2036, up from ~$36.5B. Medicaid: ~10.0M users × ~$140 net after statutory rebates × 12 ≈ $16.8B, of which ~$11B is federal at a ~65% blended match. Retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin and MariTide sit on few Part D formularies, mostly as tier-5 exceptions.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month across 150+ brands. India's export registration for B2C pharmaceutical parcels took effect in 2035. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials run $25–60 through research-peptide fronts. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 40–75 and BRL 150–260. India and China supply ~70% of world volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continued: TrumpRx maintenance prices are now $169 for the Wegovy pill, $149 for Foundayo and $199–249 for injectable Wegovy/Zepbound. Retatrutide fell $299 → $279 and MariTide $219 → $199. Starting oral doses stayed at $149, and the $1,349 list price is untouched. Oral-first step therapy in Medicare and Medicaid pushed orals to ~58% of users. Employer weight coverage slipped from 29% to 28% as some employers carved out Medicare-eligible retirees and moved obese employees on low wages toward Medicaid. Monitored metabolic tracks hold ~7.0M, inside the 14.5M commercial users. MariTide totals ~7.4M users. Gray use fell from 15.4M to 14.5M. Older and poorer gray users moved onto Medicaid and Medicare, and Indian parcel registration thinned cheap semaglutide mail. Lean longevity users blocked by the seven-state in-person rule kept buying vials, though, and Chinese 'reta' grew to ~5M users. The share of large employers reimbursing calm/Reset platform fees through lifestyle spending accounts fell from 19% to ~12% after the anhedonia labelling.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct (bimagrumab; not an incretin)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, growth-monitoring language; barred for weight indication by statute in eleven states)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market and no new indication was approved. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out in Jun 2035 and met its primary endpoint with a modest effect (HR ~0.86). The existing obesity-plus-CVD label was retained. Lilly filed a broader sNDA for obesity without CVD in Feb 2036, and it is under standard review with no decision before 2037. Novo's phase 3 in gambling disorder read out in Nov 2036, positive on its primary endpoint; Novo says it will file in 2037. Oral amycretin and two Chinese triple agonists are in phase 3 with no US filing. Implants remain in phase 2. Bimagrumab got a cash programme ($399 with coaching) but no new indication. US net prices drift down 3–5% a year. Brands hold $149–279 in cash and $149/$245 in Medicare.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation at full doses. A new pattern comes from drug holidays: users who restart injectables at full dose after skipping two or more weeks generate a visible share of GI emergency visits.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; gastroparesis caution retained; re-titration-after-missed-doses language emphasised in 2035 labelling update.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases up with volume, especially among new Medicare obesity-route users; per-user risk unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. In the 2035 EPI bellwether a Kentucky jury found for the plaintiff on failure-to-warn for the pre-2031 period.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL continues with settlement talks.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The 2036 influx of ~12.5M obesity-route Medicare users, mostly on orals without DXA or coaching, raises the expected absolute fracture count. CMS actuaries project ~9,000 excess hip fractures a year by 2038.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab rarely covered in Part D (prior authorisation, tier 5).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults. The 2035 pooled anhedonia analysis found no excess in suicidal behaviour.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: An FDA-requested pooled analysis of randomised trials that used SHAPS/PHQ instruments (2035) put clinically meaningful anhedonia at 6.8% on weight-loss doses vs 3.1% on placebo, 9.6% on retatrutide 12 mg, and roughly dose-proportional. In about half of cases it resolved within 4–8 weeks of dose reduction or interruption. Low-dose (calm/longevity/Reset) incidence is 'not established' on the label. The NIH normal-weight cohort's 2036 interim reports ~4.5% vs ~3% unadjusted.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions section added Sep 2035 via safety labelling change, with the prevalence estimate, a dose-reduction recommendation and a Medication Guide. Not boxed. The 2034 FTC–FDA consent orders on marketing claims remain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Planned holidays of 2–6 weeks produce partial regain of ~1–3% of body weight, mostly reversed on resumption.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy coverage criteria in the CMS rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users; fat-soluble deficiency tied to EPI. Lean gray users rarely get panels. Medicaid users get them more often than gray users did.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual panel language retained; CMS rule cites it in coverage criteria.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide. Partial recovery in about half after 12+ months off. Tirzepatide 6-year excess is still non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling; tirzepatide under continued review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up. ~19M current users have a BMI under 30. Cycling and holiday effects on bone and pancreas are still poorly characterised. No new confirmed signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone/growth PMRs continue; NIH normal-weight cohort reported first interim (2036).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~58,000. No repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen cluster. 'Reta' vial potency still ranges from 0 to over 300% of label, and ~20% test endotoxin-positive. Poison-centre calls have plateaued at ~7× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and India's 2035 parcel registration in place; personal-importation enforcement still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 48-month liraglutide PMR (2035) shows the ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit persisting, with partial catch-up in a minority of those who stopped. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label monitoring retained; eleven-state under-12 bans unchanged; EMA specialist-initiation rule retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: About 36% of users report at least one deliberate holiday in the past year (2036 KFF poll). Risks include GI events on full-dose restart and loss of glycaemic control in diabetic users who skip. Effects on bone and lean mass from repeated short cycles are unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Re-titration guidance in labels; no specific warning; ADA and Endocrine Society issued holiday protocols (2036).

food_and_beverage.state: About 55% of households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volume is down ~17% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~15%. Medicaid coverage broke zip-code planning: value multipacks are now losing volume in the low-income zips where they were the hedge, and Walmart and Dollar General are cutting multipack facings in the Delta and Appalachia. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down. Protein lines and the longevity supplement aisle grow. Weekend 'holiday' baskets show measurable Friday–Saturday indulgence spikes in high-density zips.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume is down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. AUD prescribing rose through Medicaid. Holiday weekends partly offset losses: on-premise sales concentrate in 'off-weekend' nights. Two more regional breweries closed. Non-alcoholic drinks are near 6% of volume.

restaurants.state: Weekday traffic is down. Weekend traffic in user-dense metros is spiky around holidays, and Austin and Charlotte venues sell 'off-weekend' tasting nights. Late-night QSR traffic in low-income markets fell as Medicaid replaced interruption-prone gray supply. Portion tiers are standard.

apparel.state: Plus-size keeps shrinking. A national plus-size chain closed 30% of stores in 2035. Low-income size runs are converging downward. Muscle-cut tailoring and structured athletic wear carry premium margins, and the 'soft-small' Medicaid body is served by mass basics.

fitness.state: Strength training and DXA-plus-coaching memberships ($250–450) grow among the top third. Bimagrumab-plus-coaching cash bundles ($399 drug plus $200–300 coaching) appeared in 2035. Budget chains' lean-mass add-ons are flat, because Medicaid and Medicare users rarely join. Lean mass is now the most visible class marker in a body.

insurance.state: Commercial weight coverage is 28%, with pharmacy trend ~+5%. Part D plans absorbed ~12.5M new obesity-route users: the 2036 base beneficiary premium rose to the statutory growth cap, and plans lean hard on oral-first step therapy. Medicare Advantage plans market DXA benefits to attract healthier users. Adherence premium differentials persist, but vendors added 'clinician-approved holiday' codes after the label change.

pharma.state: Volume is up ~25% and US net price per user down ~8%. Novo gained most from oral-first public formularies. Lilly holds the retatrutide cash tier and the dementia filing. Amgen's MariTide is concentrated in employer tracks. Label-change and EPI litigation costs keep rising. Sportsbook operators still cite 'pharmacological headwinds', though less loudly.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness no longer signals class, because Medicaid made it a $0–$4 pill. What signals class is what the thinness is made of. Thin with scanned muscle, coached and on retatrutide plus bimagrumab is the top third. Thin and soft with small arms, on an oral from public coverage, is the 'Medicaid build'. Lean, never obese, with a biological-age printout is longevity. Regained or mid-cycle now reads as uninsured in a non-expansion state, or as gray-market.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Charlotte and Austin the uniform is shoulders and a DXA percentile, and 'I train, I don't just take it' is the boast. In Columbus the Medicaid pill flattened the visible weight gap between shift leads and line staff; the gap moved into arms and gait. In the Delta, older users shifted from gray 'reta' to Medicaid orals, losing less weight but holding it. Working-age uninsured adults in Texas and Georgia are the new visibly heavy class, and politicians in both parties now name them.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Weekday meals are small and protein-led. Holiday weekends brought back a compressed feast culture: Friday dinners, Sunday brunches and birthdays timed to a skipped dose. Bread Alone claims ~900 congregations. Church potlucks in Ohio report 'everyone's on, so no one notices'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'holiday schedule' fields. 'Lean-mass verified' remains a premium tier. 'Reset' badges lost some cachet after the label. Couples coordinate holidays for anniversaries and conception attempts.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: After the label, appetite and desire came back as signs of being yourself, felt on holiday and measured against the flat week. Upper-tier users talk about 'dosing for the week, living on the weekend'. Unmuted gained members and an FDA citation to point to. The MAHA wing splits between celebrating the label and attacking the Medicare expansion as pharma welfare.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The label states 6.8% vs 3.1% placebo at weight-loss doses and 9.6% on retatrutide 12 mg. Applied to ~98M users, that is roughly 3.5–4M people with drug-attributable clinically meaningful anhedonia at any time, most on full doses. Low-dose incidence is 'not established', with ~4.5% unadjusted in the NIH interim. Subjective complaint runs far higher: ~41% of users in a 2036 KFF poll said the drug made things 'feel less', and ~36% reported a deliberate holiday or step-down in the past year.
interior_life.framing: Clinicians call it a labelled, dose-related adverse effect managed by step-down or holiday. Users call it 'the flat' and holidays 'coming up'. Employers dropped 'steadiness' from benefit materials. Unmuted calls the label vindication. Platforms bound by the consent orders say nothing, and their reviews talk about 'finding your dose'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employment counsel now advise against using adherence data in promotion decisions. In Mar 2036 the Southern District of Ohio denied the call-centre operator's motion to dismiss, citing the new label in finding a plausible ADA 'regarded as' theory. Calm/Reset LSA reimbursement fell from ~19% to ~12% of large employers. Adherence premium differentials remain legal, which produces friction: a doctor-advised holiday can break verification, and vendors patch it with holiday codes that require clinician sign-off. Columbus 3PLs quietly stopped circulating track-enrollee promotion stats.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Weekend culture re-spiked. Bars, sportsbooks and clubs see 'off-weekend' surges, and Sunday NFL handle per account partly recovered in Ohio and New Jersey. 'Coming up' became a music and video genre about the first unmedicated weekend. The ambient and slow-game market is flat. Stand-up moved from the flat audience to the holiday audience.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule holidays for sex, conception and fights they have put off. Therapists report a new pattern: partners who are tender on holidays and absent on dosing weeks. Desire mismatch remains the top complaint, but it is now treated as adjustable, and some therapists write holiday plans with prescribers.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The anhedonia label became a talking point in the Part D premium fight. Fiscal conservatives and MAHA legislators cite it against the CMS rule, and progressive and senior groups defend coverage while demanding DXA and mental-health screening. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. Unmuted held its first national convening in Cleveland.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products and coverage, restrictive on marketing and the young. CMS reclassified chronic-obesity drugs out of the statutory weight-loss exclusion by rule. FDA added class anhedonia labelling. No state enacted, repealed or amended incretin law in the window.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Medicaid coverage of anti-obesity medications for chronic obesity is mandatory under the CMS rule from Oct 2035, and Part D coverage since Jan 2036, both behind prior authorisation and oral-first step therapy. Manufacturer price agreements are $149 orals and $245 injectables. Litigation by a coalition of trade groups challenging the rule's statutory reading is pending in the D.C. Circuit. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Part D and Medicaid PA requires BMI documentation and 6-month progress notes, a new public-sector data stream. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Wellness vendors still receive clinic, PBM and telehealth data under consent, now with holiday codes.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE is unchanged. The Army oral pilot continues. DOT's 2033 guidance stands, and medical examiners now ask about the anhedonia Medication Guide on intake forms without changing fitness standards.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C parcel export registration took effect in 2035 and Indian semaglutide mail volume fell by roughly a third. Chinese 'reta' via research-peptide fronts continues. Public formularies' reliance on Novo orals made oral semaglutide API capacity in Denmark and North Carolina a quiet Medicare supply-security issue.

events.event: CMS finalises a rule ending the weight-loss exclusion for drugs used to treat chronic obesity; Medicaid must cover them from October and Part D plans from January 2036, at manufacturer-agreed prices of $149 for pills and $245 for injectables

Lilly's dementia confirmatory trial meets its primary endpoint with a modest effect; the company files to extend the label to obese adults without heart disease, with no FDA decision expected before 2037
FDA adds reward blunting to every incretin label: 6.8% of users on weight-loss doses vs 3.1% on placebo, nearly 10% on high-dose retatrutide, with advice to reduce the dose or pause
About 12.5 million Medicare beneficiaries obtain incretins through the new obesity route in its first year; Part D premiums rise to the statutory cap and plans require pills before injections

Ohio federal judge refuses to dismiss call-centre agent's suit over promotions tied to monitored drug tracks, citing the new label; a benefits survey finds employers reimbursing 'calm' fees fell from 19% to 12%
KFF poll finds 36% of users took a deliberate drug holiday in the past year; DXA-and-coaching memberships and $399 bimagrumab bundles grow among top earners while public-plan users go unscanned

open_tensions: Part D incretin spend is near $63B a year and premiums are at the statutory cap. The trade-group challenge to the CMS rule sits in the D.C. Circuit, and Congress has neither ratified nor blocked it. The default payer rests on an administrative reading that a court or a new administration could reverse.

The label tells users to step down or pause, while the 30% adherence-premium guidance still rewards unbroken verified fills. Holiday codes depend on clinician sign-off, and the Ohio ADA suit now heads toward discovery on how employers used adherence data.

Thinness spread to the bottom third, and the class gap moved into muscle and bone. About 12.5 million new Medicare obesity-route users are mostly on unscanned orals at a hip-fracture HR of ~1.3, while bimagrumab and coaching stay a $600-a-month cash tier.

About nineteen million users without obesity, largely cash or gray and outside public coverage criteria, have a low-dose anhedonia rate the label calls 'not established'. The uninsured working-age obese in non-expansion states are now the most visible group left out.

prose.headline: Medicare Pays, the Label Says 'Flat', and America Takes the Weekend Off
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 more than one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, about ninety-eight million people, and nearly half have tried one. This time the jump came from the government. In April 2035 CMS finalised a rule saying that drugs used to treat chronic obesity are not the 'weight-loss agents' Medicare and Medicaid law lets them exclude. Medicaid had to start paying that October, and Part D plans in January. Congress never voted on it. Some twelve and a half million Medicare beneficiaries came in through the new door in its first year, and Medicaid users roughly tripled. Public programmes now pay for more users than employers, cash or the mail.

They pay a manufacturer-agreed $149 a month for pills and $245 for injections, and plans make patients try the pill first. Part D spending on these drugs is approaching $63 billion a year. Premiums rose to the legal cap, and a trade-group lawsuit claiming CMS read the statute wrong is waiting in the D.C. Circuit. Cash prices kept drifting down. The Wegovy pill is $169 at maintenance, Lilly's retatrutide $279 and MariTide $199. Starting pills are still $149, and the box price is still $1,349. Employers covering weight loss slipped to 28 percent.

In September 2035 the FDA did something it had avoided for four years. It put reward blunting on every incretin label: 6.8 percent of users at weight-loss doses against 3.1 percent on placebo, nearly ten percent on high-dose retatrutide, with advice to lower the dose or pause. The label added no box and no new restrictions, only a number. The number changed how people talk. Two in five users tell pollsters the drug makes things feel less. More than a third took a deliberate holiday last year: a skipped week before a wedding, a weekend off for a playoff game, a month off to try for a baby. Doctors' societies wrote holiday protocols. Emergency rooms learned to recognise the patient who restarted at full dose on Monday.

The label also reached the workplace. Employers that had reimbursed 'calm' subscriptions as a perk quietly stopped, from nineteen percent of large firms to twelve. In March a federal judge in Ohio refused to dismiss a call-centre agent's claim that promotions favoured workers in monitored drug tracks, and the ruling cited the label. The rule that lets employers charge up to thirty percent more to workers whose adherence is not verified still stands, so a doctor-advised pause can cost money. Vendors now sell 'clinician-approved holiday' codes to fix that.

Bodies still sort, though the sorting has moved. A Medicaid pill made thinness cheap, so thinness stopped meaning anything. In Charlotte and Austin the uniform is shoulders and a DXA percentile, maintained with retatrutide, a $399 muscle-preserving antibody and a coach. On the Columbus freight corridor the weight gap between shift leads and line workers has closed, and the difference shows in arms and in how people climb stairs. The newly visible heavy class is uninsured working adults in Texas and Georgia, too poor for $149 and not poor enough for Medicaid. Actuaries expect several thousand extra hip fractures a year among unscanned older pill users before the decade ends.

The gray market shrank slightly. Older users moved onto public coverage, and India's parcel rules thinned the cheap mail. Lean longevity users locked out of telehealth by state in-person rules keep buying Chinese vials. Spirits fell further. Weekends got loud again: bars, sportsbooks and brunch places fill on off-weekends and sit quiet on dosing weeks. No new drug arrived and no new use was approved. The country is medicated on weekdays and comes off the drug on weekends.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rosalind Akers, forty-four, takes her Wegovy pill at 5:40 with half a glass of water and waits thirty minutes before coffee. Ohio Medicaid, four-dollar copay. The pharmacy stapled the new Medication Guide to the bag in October, and she read the boxed-off paragraph twice in the car.

Her first client is Mr. Delacroix, seventy-nine, on Zepbound since January under the Medicare thing. She steadies him on the stairs. His arms are thinner than hers. He jokes that he's 'turning into a coat hanger,' and she writes it down for the nurse.

At lunch her cousin Tasha texts from Memphis: a photo of a vial, label in English and Chinese. Got two more months of reta before I switch. Rosalind sends back a thumbs-up and doesn't mean it.

Her son Marcus, ten, eats a second sandwich in the kitchen after school. The pediatrician said wait until twelve, it's the law here. He's fine. He's fine.

At six her daughter calls about Saturday, the quinceañera practice, and asks if Mom's 'going off this weekend.' Rosalind says she'll ask Dr. Patel. Dr. Patel said last month a day or two won't matter with the pill. She's not sure that's what she wants. Last time she skipped she cried at a car commercial and felt, for an afternoon, enormous.

At nine she sits on the porch with a beer she doesn't finish. The neighbour's TV is on the game. Somebody scores, and the whole street cheers but her.

first_errors: s5-L1-r05-j1: least_plausible_claims/1/quote: not found verbatim in the candidate ('About 12.5 million Medicare beneficiaries obtain incretins through the new obesity route in its first year; Part D plans'); copy it character for character

least_plausible_claims.quote: Upper-tier users talk about 'dosing for the week, living on the weekend'.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the weekend-holiday culture depends on reward returning within a day or two off a drug with roughly week-long half-life (semaglutide). The candidate's own label data says anhedonia resolves in 4–8 weeks of reduction or interruption, and the prose has Dr. Patel saying 'a day or two won't matter with the pill'.

least_plausible_claims.quote: the company files to extend the label to obese adults without heart disease, with no FDA decision expected before 2037
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: this event dates the filing to June 2035, but pipeline_note says Lilly filed the sNDA in Feb 2036. The two disagree, and a filing in the same month as the readout is also implausibly fast.

Magnitude: about 19M of 98M users have BMI under 30, so roughly 79M users have BMI of 30 or more. Add the 14% of adults who are obese and have never used (~39M) and the total is over 100M obese adults, against about 84M implied by 30.3%. The 2034 parent has the same inconsistency, and the candidate repeats it.
